claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages per the strategies in this guide, which improve reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), even if not a valid semantic version.
An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically with per-language SDKs published to feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type; multi-package repositories must release in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected, shipping together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend a single monorepo with one giant package for all components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every release versions every component the same way, violating semver.
In the example sequence, an enhancement to ComponentA yields v1.1.0 and a breaking change to ComponentB yields v2.0.0 for the package.
Cross-referenced pages exist: packages concepts, components concepts, packaging-components anchors, Private Registry, pulumi_package_publish, publishing-packages.
